page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-2560s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 2560 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in specific memory and single-core operations. The server achieves a top-tier rating in large-block uncached memory write bandwidth, registering 170.21 GB/sec, and a strong rating in large-block uncached memory read bandwidth at 339.94 GB/sec. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, scoring 2927.78. Multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and database operations fall within the average tier. Memory performance is further validated by a strong PassMark memory score of 2944.76. Large-scale data decompression and static web serving throughput also maintain average tier metrics.

With its dedicated CPU allocation and substantial 128.0 GB memory capacity, this instance offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of shared-core configurations. The inclusion of a large 2560 GB NVMe SSD provides a cost-efficient storage-to-compute ratio, eliminating the need for external block storage attachments for large datasets. This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-optimized databases, caching layers such as Redis, data-intensive web serving, and moderate-scale multi-threaded processing tasks.
